note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative. The two scenes share every text; only the supplied status of the intermediate premise (stated / left unstated) differs. No winner, score or conclusion is drawn.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Fictional shed key: A states “Whoever holds the shed key locked the shed last”, B leaves it unstated. A’s printed card is latched into the walk; B’s pencil card stays loose in its pocket and is read with the magnifier.

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: Substantive alternative: a fictional library return with the roles swapped — A leaves the premise unstated, B states it — and different shared facts, issue and assumption.

params.facts: The blue umbrella was left at the library desk
params.rules: Items left at the desk go to lost property at closing
params.conclusion: The umbrella went to lost property
issues: Did the desk close at the usual time that day?

scenarioA.label: Premise left unstated
scenarioA.caption: The note only says fact, then conclusion

scenarioB.label: Premise stated
scenarioB.caption: The note also writes the step in between

params.changedFact: Whether the note writes “Items left at the desk go to lost property at closing”

comparisonLabels.neutral: Two supplied notes side by side — neither is marked better or worse

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long fact, premise and conclusion texts, long scenario labels and captions, long changed-fact and neutral note, four shared facts, two issues and two assumptions.

params.facts: The only key to the garden shed was found in the inside pocket of Jo’s winter coat the next morning
params.rules: Whoever is holding the only shed key the next morning is the person who locked the shed the night before
params.conclusion: Jo is the person who locked the garden shed on the night before the key was found
issues: Who else could have opened or locked the shed that evening without the key?
Was the coat left unattended in the hall overnight?
assumptions: There is only one key and no other way to lock the shed
The coat was not lent to anyone that evening

scenarioA.label: The argument states its intermediate premise
scenarioA.caption: The step between the fact and the conclusion is written out

scenarioB.label: The argument leaves the premise unstated
scenarioB.caption: The same step is not written; only fact and conclusion appear

params.changedFact: Only whether the step “whoever holds the only key locked the shed” is written in the argument
sharedFacts: the same fact card and wording
the same conclusion card and wording
the same board, hinges and magnifier

comparisonLabels.guide: This is the only circumstance that differs

issues: ¿Quién más pudo abrir el cobertizo esa tarde?
